pull.title: Warn on and add missing `[[noreturn]]`
pull.body:
Missing `[[noreturn]]` attributes can cause compiler false positives and other issues; see discussion in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35896#discussion_r3726612556. Add missing attributes, and turn on compiler warnings.

Some `[[noreturn]]` additions may appear redundant, however they suppress warnings for various compiler versions, see discussion in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35911#discussion_r4658191746, and could be dropped in future, when support for those compilers is removed.

Related:
https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/pull/339.
https://github.com/bitcoin-core/leveldb-subtree/pull/64.
https://github.com/arun11299/cpp-subprocess/pull/132.

comments.body:
> https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-4.2.2/gcc/Warning-Options.html

Your documentation is about 20 years out of date. The [modern docs](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Warning-Options.html#index-Wsuggest-attribute_003d) say:
> Warn about functions that might be candidates for attributes pure, const, noreturn, malloc or returns_nonnull. The compiler only warns for functions visible in other compilation units or (in the case of pure and const) if it cannot prove that the function returns normally. A function returns normally if it doesn’t contain an infinite loop or return abnormally by throwing, calling abort or trapping. This analysis requires option -fipa-pure-const, which is enabled by default at -O and higher. Higher optimization levels improve the accuracy of the analysis.

nit: it's a bit awkward to mark a `virtual` method as `[[noreturn]]` when an override can be implemented to return.

The libmultiprocess generated `ProxyClient` method overrides can return. I don't think anything in-tree calls `makeMiningOld2` (or `submitSolutionOld7`) via IPC, but if that changes, a newer client (with `noreturn`) that calls an older server (that may return) can cause UB. The IPC interface is experimental, but at the same time the only reason we have these `Old` functions to handle version mismatches gracefully. Perhaps it makes sense to just not mark these kinds of functions as `virtual`?
